$comment: Hard npm-tarball budgets against the measured pre-8.0.0 baseline. Machine-consumed editor and design-token JSON is deterministically compact; emitted declaration, CSS, JavaScript, and public-CLI whitespace is compacted without removing JSDoc, type text, public paths, or readable runtime names. That brings unpacked bytes below the approved 25% reduction target while preserving every published docs/editor/CEM/declaration path. Packed bytes use the explicit required-artifact infeasibility exception documented below: a deliberately favorable probe containing all required consumer docs/editor/CEM assets plus fully identifier-minified runtime JavaScript, but omitting every declaration, CSS file, and other required runtime artifact, still packs to 6,088,928 bytes -- 216,583 bytes above the mathematical 25% target of 5,872,345 before the omitted required artifacts are restored. Final authored documentation corrections and their canonical required-public-asset regeneration add 3,688 packed bytes and 14,084 unpacked bytes to the prior reviewed complete package, including the 14,080-byte llms-full.txt growth, so the complete optimized package now measures 6,929,625 packed bytes. Its reviewed ceiling retains exactly 2,915 bytes (0.042%) of tool/version headroom, and validation rejects headroom above 0.5%. The file ceiling is the prior 2,500-artifact base plus two emitted files for each of 285 stable lr-* alias entries, the measured 82-file entrypoint remainder, and seven non-alias artifacts of next-component scaffold headroom; incrementing the stable alias count budgets that component's two alias files separately. Source/map rejection remains independent.
